profile.reading:
This is a confirmed, currently operating facility of 1GServers, a bare-metal dedicated-server, colocation, and cloud VPS hosting provider, at 3719 East La Salle Street in Phoenix, Arizona -- the address on 1GServers' own site matches this registry's OpenStreetMap-derived address exactly. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly based on the exact address match.

1GServers markets dedicated servers with port speeds from 1 up to 40 Gbps, pre-configured auto-deploy server options, colocation services, and cloud VPS hosting from this Phoenix location, positioning itself as a budget-oriented alternative to larger enterprise colocation providers. The company advertises redundant power, physical security controls, and a stated 100% uptime service level agreement for this facility, per its own site.

This is a smaller, single-site hosting provider rather than a multi-campus wholesale or hyperscale operator; 1GServers does not publish a specific IT capacity in megawatts, technical square footage, or year-opened date for this Phoenix facility in the materials found this session, consistent with the more limited public disclosure typical of smaller regional hosting providers compared to the large operators tracked elsewhere in this registry. Phoenix has grown into a major US data center market over the past decade, driven by relatively low land and power costs and a large regional grid footprint, providing context for why a budget hosting provider like 1GServers would locate here alongside much larger operators such as Iron Mountain, EdgeConneX, and CyrusOne, all separately tracked in this registry.

reading.body:
The operator of this Phoenix facility is not published. A building named 1GServers appears at this address in OpenStreetMap, verified in September 2026, but no website, spec page, or operator-level information has been located despite exhausted research. Without published specifications for power capacity, floor space, cooling, or power source, the campus cannot be assessed against the criteria that determine relevance to AI infrastructure.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only four publish power capacity figures totaling 512 MW. This facility is not among those four publishers and therefore does not appear in the state's published capacity ranking. Whether 1GServers is operational, dormant, repurposed, or planned for data center use cannot be determined from available sources.

To assess whether this campus matters to AI scaling requires finding the operator and obtaining published specifications. The address exists and the name suggests compute services, but without operator confirmation or technical details, the facility remains an open research item.
